look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Examine the flower head from both sides. The yellow ray florets have reddish-maroon veins underneath, and the head is cupped by broad overlapping green involucral bracts (phyllaries). Look for a dark maroon disk and soft, often lyrately lobed gray-green basal leaves. Smell may be chocolate-like, especially in the morning, but do not identify from fragrance or yellow rays alone.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Perennial forb with leafy basal growth and ascending flowering stalks; variable low mounding to taller growth.

key_traits.label: Leaves attachment
key_traits.text: Leaves alternate, often concentrated near base, softly hairy, gray-green, obovate to spatulate or lyrately lobed; terminal leaf portion often larger than small lower lobes. Inspect the actual plant rather than assume all leaves are deeply divided.

key_traits.label: Flower reproductive
key_traits.text: Solitary radiate heads on stalks, usually several yellow ray florets with maroon veins on the lower surface, surrounding a reddish-maroon disk. Broad green overlapping phyllaries form a conspicuous cup below the head.

key_traits.label: Fruit seed
key_traits.text: At fruiting, distinctive green cup-like head structure persists as rays fall; confirm mature cypsela and associated bracts in a macro view.

key_traits.label: Stem bud
key_traits.text: Hairy, often longitudinally striped flowering stems; check stem and leaf attachment on live material.

names: Berlandiera texana — may share yellow rays and dark disk; check more strongly clasping stem leaves and detailed head/leaf structures, not scent alone.
Berlandiera pumila — similar chocolate-flower relatives; compare leaf dissection, pubescence, phyllaries and mature fruit with a regional key.
Thelesperma spp. — yellow ray or rayless heads can confuse at a glance; check leaves and green cup-like involucral bracts.
lookalikes.differences: Combine ray underside maroon venation, green cup-like overlapping phyllaries, maroon disk and leaf shape. One yellow head is not enough.
